occurrences.claim_id: How we designed the experiment/numPubBlocks/1
occurrences.section: How we designed the experiment
occurrences.context: Changing a hyperparameter is not the only reason RMSE changes. A different random split can make a training problem slightly easier or harder. We therefore repeated planned configurations across \numPubBlocks{} split seeds, called \term{blocks}. This allowed the statistical model to separate systematic hyperparameter effects from partition-related nuisance variation. Figure~\ref{fig:blocking} shows center-point observations: the configuration is nominally the same, yet the block means move.

occurrences.context:
For each trial we recorded development validation RMSE and single-row CPU prediction latency. The initial measurements used warmup and 
umPubPrimaryCalls{} timed calls per prediction interface. The repeated searches used a cheaper 
umPubOnlineCalls{}-call online measurement after 
umPubOnlineWarmups{} warmup calls. Final benchmark verification used 
umPubPrimarySessions{} separately randomized sessions under the warmed 
umPubPrimaryCalls{}-call protocol. Standard 	exttt{predict} also includes data-wrapper overhead: the interface comparison measured 
umRevInterfaceOverhead\,$\pm$\,
umRevInterfaceOverheadSd\,$\mu$s more than 	exttt{inplace\_predict}. Search-time latency and benchmark verification latency are therefore distinct measurements and are never treated as interchangeable.
